page.layout: One page of text: a decorative rule at the top, then a centred heading, a verse passage with a large initial F, an italic line and a name below the verse, right-aligned, and a Greek line beneath. No margin notes. A library stamp sits below the text and is not transcribed.

main_text.l: undis, Omnia pervertit, Jovam post tergora mittens,
Cœptum est lymphatæ confinia dogmata menti.
Ergo opus est seutica [?]: justis hanc plectite flagris
O Socii! Injectis frenate sophisma lupatis!
Præstes, qui tanti mensuram nominis implet.
Hinc exurget honos, hinc tempora laurea cinget.
Christe, Dei Fili, tu nostram, dirige cymbam,
Da te Navarchâ felicia littora tangat
Nostra ratis: Laudémque tuam cantabimus usque!

l.i: ic Candidatorum suóque nomine ponit ac vovet

page.notes: The initial F of the first line is a large drop capital, joined to "oeda" as "Foeda". Line 6 reads "seutica" as printed; it probably means "scutica", so it is marked [?]. The Greek signature line is hard to read and is uncertain. A ghosted mirror image of a heading from the reverse side appears at the top right and is not transcribed. A library stamp is present and not transcribed.
